messages.author: 4b06c0bae2d1991d
messages.subject: mirtCAT timing
parts: hopefully an easy question ---- how does mirtCAT measure time? For max_time (in the test design) or item_time (in the person results), is it based off of local computer time, or based off of time at the host server?

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: mirtCAT timing
parts:
The time is always local, and is based on when the user clicks the action button (initialises and terminates at the same time). If the interface were hosted on the server, then the time would be taken off the server (i..e, whatever computer is actually running the mirtCAT() function). 

Phil

messages.author: 4b06c0bae2d1991d
messages.subject: Re: mirtCAT timing
parts:
Thanks for the quick reply. That's a little disappointing though, for running timed tests on a remote server. Then the timing would be subject to speed of internet traffic and could be highly variable depending on who is taking the test. I suppose the only way around that is to run the test on the local computer as opposed to a central server.
Aaron

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: mirtCAT timing
parts:
That's true, but honestly I can't think of a good way around it. It's possible to try and get the front-end user's browser to sent time information, but that could be difficult (and would even be subject to clock changes on the local computer OS....which obviously would mess with everything). For series CAT usage it's best to do things locally. Remote CAT are, in my opinion, more of an exploratory/not high stakes method (even things like security of item content go out the window with remote hosting).

Phil
